key_insight: Explainable machine learning on early Parkinson’s disease data identified age and baseline cognitive score as the strongest predictors of later mild cognitive impairment and postural instability.
clinical_relevance: These interpretable models could support earlier risk stratification and more personalized follow-up for people with early Parkinson’s disease.
method: Used Explainable Boosting Machines (EBM), an interpretable machine learning approach
Compared a minimal clinico-demographic feature set with an extended multimodal set
Analyzed predictors for progression to mild cognitive impairment and postural instability in two independent early-PD cohorts
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparable predictive performance for minimal and extended datasets across two independent cohorts, with age and Montreal Cognitive Assessment score emerging as top features.
watch_item: The findings are predictive rather than causal, so external validation and careful clinical integration are still needed before routine use.
paper_title: Explainable machine learning identifies predictors for postural instability and cognitive impairment in early Parkinsons Disease
